summary: Learn Cisco SDA operations, segmentation and troubleshooting through campus fabric scenarios. Review the course and plan your training.
lede: Software-defined access (SDA) training is for network engineers and infrastructure administrators who support campus fabric networks. Through practical exercises, it covers assessing underlay readiness, tracing LISP control-plane and VXLAN forwarding behaviour, using Catalyst Center workflows and assurance information to isolate faults, and documenting segmentation and change decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for network professionals who support Cisco campus switching and need to work with fabric architecture, segmentation and operations.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of Ethernet switching, VLANs, IPv4 addressing and routing is expected. Familiarity with Cisco campus networks and Cisco IOS XE configuration is useful. Programming is not required; exercises use network diagrams, configuration excerpts and operational scenarios.
